title: Number of Subarrays That Match a Pattern II
summary: Given an integer array nums and a pattern array of -1, 0, and 1, count the number of subarrays of size m+1 in nums that match the pattern by comparing adjacent elements according to the pattern's values.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a pattern array of -1, 0, and 1, count the number of subarrays of size m+1 in nums that match the pattern by comparing adjacent elements according to the pattern's values.
constraints: nums may contain up to one million positive integers; pattern is nonempty and shorter than nums.
Convert adjacent comparisons to -1, 0, or 1 and count every overlapping occurrence of pattern.
Return the count in O(n+m) time.
reference_solution:
def count_matching_comparison_subarrays_large(nums,pattern):
    text=[(right>left)-(right<left) for left,right in zip(nums,nums[1:])]
    prefix=[0]*len(pattern)
    for index in range(1,len(pattern)):
        length=prefix[index-1]
        while length and pattern[index]!=pattern[length]:length=prefix[length-1]
        if pattern[index]==pattern[length]:length+=1
        prefix[index]=length
    answer=length=0
    for value in text:
        while length and value!=pattern[length]:length=prefix[length-1]
        if value==pattern[length]:length+=1
        if length==len(pattern):answer+=1;length=prefix[length-1]
    return answer

hints: The problem is ordinary pattern matching after mapping adjacent numbers to comparison signs.
Build a KMP prefix table for pattern and scan the sign sequence without materializing substrings.
Advance or fall back by prefix links; on a full match increment and fall back to allow overlaps.
KMP’s state is the longest pattern prefix matching the processed suffix, so every and only full comparison-pattern occurrence is counted in linear time.
